bug_semantics: The CMS controller admitted a backend user possessing any one CMS Theme Editor permission, but its AJAX handlers trusted the request-controlled template type and did not re-check the permission mapped to that type. A pages-only user could therefore open, create, save, delete, commit, or reset partials, layouts, content, or assets by crafting the handler parameters. The constructor also registered every template widget, including AssetList, for every admitted CMS user; AssetList's upload path processed a file without first binding the request to the active theme, so a user without cms.manage_assets could reach an unauthorized upload into the active theme's assets.
flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 introduced the exploitable design as new code: modules/cms/controllers/Index.php used the section-wide cms.* gate, instantiated every TemplateList and AssetList unconditionally, and dispatched request-supplied type values into load/create/save/delete operations without a type-specific authorization check. The same commit introduced AssetList.php with constructor-time checkUploadPostback() upload processing and no validateRequestTheme() call in that upload path, while expanding modules/cms/ServiceProvider.php to register distinct cms.manage_content/assets/pages/layouts permissions. Its parent had only a skeletal CMS ServiceProvider and had neither Index.php nor AssetList.php, so the permission boundary and bypass surface first coexist in this commit.

evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-5c4f-9pq9-6c77 states affected winter/wn-cms-module versions are <=1.2.12 and first patched is 1.2.13; it identifies Cms\Controllers\Index handlers, unconditional AssetList registration, and AssetList::onUpload as the affected surfaces. Fix inspection: `git show 164c62524e8abc153d09c6c35916278bdb746a2b -- modules/cms/controllers/Index.php modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php` shows per-permission widget registration, validateRequestType() calls in index_onOpenTemplate/onSave/onCreateTemplate/onDeleteTemplates/onDelete/onCommit/onReset, the type-to-permission mapping, and validateRequestTheme() at the start of onUpload; the commit's added permission tests explicitly deny every mismatched granted-permission/target-type pair. Origin tracing: `git log -L 53,58:modules/cms/controllers/Index.php 164c625^` reaches 55848e400cea002491a29820e5387bce0dd44362, which merely replaces the already-permissive cms.* gate with the explicit five-permission list, then reaches 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 where Index.php is added from /dev/null. `git log -L 147,152:modules/cms/controllers/Index.php 164c625^` independently reaches 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 for the unguarded request type passed to loadTemplate. Blame at the fix parent attributes unconditional `new AssetList($this, 'assetList')`, the handler bodies, the request type flow, and the original upload body to 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5. Historical source at that BIC shows Index.php's cms.* controller gate, all four TemplateList instances plus AssetList registered without permission checks, and onSave/index_onOpenTemplate using request types after only theme validation; AssetList::__construct calls checkUploadPostback(), whose upload body lacks validateRequestTheme(). Later c03fd66aeb8a6f10290381a76db0867fabe881e6 changes that existing postback processor into public onUpload(), but does not originate the already-reachable unauthorized asset upload mechanism. Direct parent verification: `git rev-parse 71a5dd67^` returns d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827; `git cat-file -e d412ea6:modules/cms/controllers/Index.php` and the equivalent AssetList.php lookup both fail because the paths are absent, while the parent's ServiceProvider.php is only a skeletal register/boot class and contains no CMS navigation or granular permission registrations. Thus the complete vulnerable mechanism is absent in the immediate parent. The BIC is a normal single-parent repository commit; line history terminates at /dev/null there and exposes no constituent member commits to decompose. Version boundary: v1.2.12 resolves to b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313 and v1.2.13 to e09c8d3526f3583cb6c3476a021b885088ecd4bd. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 71a5dd67... v1.2.12^{}` succeeds; the same check for 164c6252... in v1.2.12 fails and in v1.2.13 succeeds. `git grep validateRequestType v1.2.12 -- modules/cms/controllers/Index.php` has no match, whereas v1.2.13 has guards at every advisory-named handler and defines the validator; AssetList.php at v1.2.12 has no upload-site validateRequestTheme call, while v1.2.13 has it at onUpload. reasoning: The security boundary existed from the first public implementation, not from the later textual form of the five-item requiredPermissions array. In 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 the CMS module simultaneously defined granular per-template permissions and exposed one controller guarded only by cms.*. Once any one CMS permission admitted a user, server-side handlers selected the object class solely from attacker-controlled type/templateType values; UI side-menu restrictions were therefore not authorization. The same constructor always bound AssetList, and its upload processor accepted files without the theme check used by its other mutations. Commit 55848e400cea002491a29820e5387bce0dd44362 is not the BIC: its parent is already vulnerable, and its change from cms.* to the explicit five permissions only excludes manage_themes-only users while retaining any-one-permission entry. Commit c03fd66aeb8a6f10290381a76db0867fabe881e6 later exposes the pre-existing upload processor as onUpload, but the unconditional widget and unvalidated upload body originated in 71a5dd67. The immediate parent d412ea685560a3ce7028346d26fd9a6559eb0827 lacks the controller and widget entirely, satisfying direct parent absence. Fix 164c62524e8abc153d09c6c35916278bdb746a2b closes the lifecycle at both layers by registering only authorized widgets, mapping each type to its required permission and enforcing it in every relevant handler, and validating the upload theme. Tag ancestry and tagged-source inspection match the advisory boundary: v1.2.12 remains vulnerable and v1.2.13 contains the fix. Finally, the only attribution considered is the BIC commit object; it is an ordinary human Sam Georges commit with no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
